page: Amazon Web Services c5d.18xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 72 vCPUs and 36 physical cores utilizing the Intel Xeon 8124M processor running at 3.4 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 144.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with 1800 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU extended instructions testing both placing in the top 25 percent of results. Memory read bandwidth is also highly efficient, with cached small-block reads reaching 3706.44 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 209.03 GB/sec, both scoring in the top tier. However, write performance is more moderate, with large-block uncached writes averaging 90.37 GB/sec. Single-core performance, including Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core CPU tests, falls within the middle 50 percent range.

The instance exhibits clear performance tradeoffs, particularly in language model tasks. While LLM prompt processing speeds for small, medium, and large models maintain average tier performance, text generation speeds are weak, falling into the bottom 25 percent with 52.33 tokens/sec for small models and 7.25 tokens/sec for medium models. This indicates a limitation for real-time generative AI workloads without dedicated GPU acceleration. Conversely, the combination of high-speed local NVMe storage and strong multi-core processing makes this instance highly effective for database operations, batch processing, and multi-threaded computational workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services c5d.18xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance featuring 72 vCPUs and 36 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8124M processor running at 3.4 GHz. It is equipped with 144.0 GB of DDR4 RAM, 1800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance demonstrates strong multi-core CPU performance and high memory read bandwidth, both ranking in the top 25 percent of benchmarks. However, it displays average single-core performance and weak LLM text generation speeds. The qualitative cost profile reflects a high-density compute resource with bundled high-speed local storage, making it suitable for database operations, multi-threaded batch processing, and distributed analytics rather than memory-intensive or generative AI workloads.
